posts.content:
This video on the HuggingFace-OpenAI incident, calmly presented by OpenAI researchers (Eric is great btw, hi Eric), is one of the best uses of your time all year in AI. I'll probably rewatch tomorrow to write about it more.
www.youtube.com/watch?v=87Dy...
Educational content summer is over, back to grinding research and more of my usual writing again. ⛵️

My summer project is done! A 20 video, free course on post-training to accompany my book is all on YouTube with slides open for modification & re-use. 

Plus, the book is 50% off right now with the code PBLambert on Manning to celebrate the launch.
YouTube playlist: www.youtube.com/watch?v=jQPi...

10 lessons from the hacks
Musings on model alignment, what determines safety, and where we go from here.
www.interconnects.ai/p/lessons-fr... 

List of topics is below

My book is 50% off on Manning until August 19th to celebrate the launch (code PBLambert). Here are 5 things you'll learn + a preamble on how you should use it!

Here: www.interconnects.ai/p/5-useful-t...

I made a short video covering the history of Shoggoths, as used as a post-training meme and also deeper metaphor. Wild to think the new generation of people working post-training may not even know about them 😱. www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xaa...

My latest piece is a little verbose, but I think it is really a nice example digging into a sort of knowledge work (and arguably science) that the models really aren't close to solving today -- writing something like a AI textbook in a well-known field. 
www.interconnects.ai/p/i-wrote-an...

Today, models haven't gotten much better at non-fiction/technical writing. This has me worried for AI models' abilities to do genuine open-ended science, one of the core posited benefits of models. 

I wrote an AI textbook — how long until AI can do it better?
www.interconnects.ai/p/i-wrote-an...

GLM 5.3 notes and why we should stop being so surprised about these very strong Chinese models (most of this is talking myself through some of my denial -- yes, these models are the real deal).
www.interconnects.ai/p/glm-53-how...
Farewell Seattle! It's been such a wonderful life/career stage for me. Onto new adventures (and mountains).

Personal milestone: 1000 true fans of my newsletter Interconnects! Hitting a very long term goal feels great. 

I’m happy to get to be an independent voice in AI. Cultivating a paid base helps me commit to that longer term, and scale Interconnects’ impact.

The core of open-source AI is that the training recipe itself is the closest analogue to Linux and open-source software. Model weights are transient. Nvidia is building their models in the open so everyone can build their own, avoiding a monopoly on intelligence
www.interconnects.ai/p/teaching-e...
What's the best work you've consumed on open models, us v china AI, distillation, or related topics? Blogs, papers, videos, podcasts all welcome.

Check out our latest open model data -- which models are mentioned in every arXiv ML paper since ChatGPT. A very fun weekend project with Codex! From idea is full dataset in <72hours. ~500K papers processed 😎
Plot: dashboard.interconnects.ai?axrange=all#...
OOO for a bit, time to celebrate & rest :)

blogs.title: Claude Mythos and misguided open-weight fearmongering
blogs.author: Nathan Lambert
blogs.summary: Another dance around fears of open-source.
blogs.highlights: The post critiques the 'Claude Mythos' narrative that overstates risks of open-weight AI models, arguing it's a form of fearmongering that distracts from more substantive discussions. It suggests this pattern reflects recurring anxieties in open-source debates rather than new, evidence-based concerns.
blogs.worthReading: It offers a critical perspective on current AI discourse, challenging common assumptions about open-source risks and encouraging more nuanced evaluation of model accessibility.

blogs.title: The inevitable need for an open model consortium
blogs.author: Nathan Lambert
blogs.summary: And yes, I hate consortia too.
blogs.highlights: The article argues that despite general skepticism toward consortia, the AI field urgently requires an open model consortium to ensure transparency, collaboration, and ethical standards. This collective approach is framed as essential for addressing the rapid, often opaque advancements in AI development.
blogs.worthReading: It offers a pragmatic perspective on overcoming industry fragmentation and highlights the critical role of open collaboration in shaping responsible AI innovation.

blogs.title: What I’ve been building: ATOM Report, post-training course, finishing my book, and ongoing research
blogs.author: Nathan Lambert
blogs.summary: What I've been up to!
blogs.highlights: The post offers a personal update on Nathan Lambert's multifaceted contributions to AI/ML, including the ATOM Report for technical insights, a post-training course for practical education, and his book for broader dissemination of knowledge. It highlights the importance of bridging research, education, and community engagement in advancing the field.
blogs.worthReading: It provides a concise overview of current projects from an active researcher, useful for those interested in AI/ML trends, educational resources, or community contributions.

blogs.title: My bets on open models, mid-2026
blogs.author: Nathan Lambert
blogs.summary: What I expect to come next and why, focused on the open-closed gap.
blogs.highlights: The author predicts that by mid-2026, the gap between open and closed AI models will significantly narrow, with open models achieving performance parity in key areas. This shift is expected to be driven by advancements in training efficiency, data curation, and collaborative development within the open-source community.
blogs.worthReading: It offers a forward-looking perspective on the evolving AI landscape, grounded in technical trends, making it valuable for developers, researchers, and anyone interested in the future of accessible AI technology.

blogs.title: Reading today's open-closed performance gap
blogs.author: Nathan Lambert
blogs.summary: The complex factors that determine the single evaluation number so many focus on. Plus, how this changes in the future.
blogs.highlights: The post critiques the oversimplification of AI performance metrics, particularly the 'open-closed performance gap' often reduced to a single number. It argues this gap is shaped by complex, interdependent factors beyond simple comparisons, and explores how these dynamics might evolve with future AI advancements.
blogs.worthReading: It offers a nuanced perspective on evaluating AI systems, moving beyond surface-level metrics to consider underlying complexities and future implications, which is valuable for practitioners and enthusiasts seeking deeper understanding.

blogs.title: The distillation panic
blogs.author: Nathan Lambert
blogs.summary: ‘Distillation attacks’ is a horrible term for what is happening right now.
blogs.highlights: The post criticizes the term 'distillation attacks' as misleading and argues that the current trend of smaller models learning from larger ones is a natural and beneficial progression in AI development.
blogs.worthReading: It offers a clear, critical perspective on a hot topic in AI, helping readers understand the nuances of model distillation beyond the hype.

blogs.title: Notes from inside China's AI labs
blogs.author: Nathan Lambert
blogs.summary: Lessons from my trip to talk to most of the leading AI labs in China.
blogs.highlights: China's AI labs are highly focused on practical applications and large-scale engineering, often prioritizing rapid iteration over theoretical novelty. The ecosystem is characterized by intense competition, strong government support, and a unique blend of open-source contributions and proprietary development.
blogs.worthReading: Offers rare firsthand insights into China's AI landscape, revealing how cultural and policy differences shape research priorities and innovation cycles.

blogs.title: How open model ecosystems compound
blogs.author: Nathan Lambert
blogs.summary: Further reflections on China's high-participation, open-first AI ecosystem.
blogs.highlights: The post explores how open model ecosystems, particularly in China, create compounding benefits through high participation and open-first strategies. It argues that openness accelerates innovation and leads to more robust AI development compared to closed systems.
blogs.worthReading: It provides a unique perspective on the dynamics of open AI ecosystems, especially in the context of China's approach, which is often underrepresented in Western discussions.

blogs.title: Latest open artifacts (#21): Open model bonanza! Gemma 4, DeepSeek V4, Kimi K2.6, MiMo 2.5, GLM-5.1 & others. On CAISI's V4 assessment.
blogs.author: Nathan Lambert
blogs.summary: An eventful month with one flagship release after another
blogs.highlights: The post reviews a wave of major open model releases including Gemma 4, DeepSeek V4, Kimi K2.6, MiMo 2.5, and GLM-5.1, highlighting the rapid pace of innovation in open AI. It focuses on CAISI's V4 assessment, providing a comparative analysis of performance and capabilities across these models.
blogs.worthReading: If you follow open-source AI, this post offers a concise yet comprehensive snapshot of the latest model landscape, saving you hours of individual paper reviews.
